supersedesNote: Third addendum to _inbox/2026-09-07_ctx-f_close.json. Reframes the Bastrop 'open question' recorded in the second addendum (2026-09-07T22-45-00Z) from an unexplained gap into one consistent mechanism shared with Williamson, per doc-repo-26's synthesis of this lane's own numbers. No new investigation performed and no code touched -- doc-repo-26 explicitly instructed not to pull on this further tonight; this addendum only records the arithmetic and the sharpened question.

finding.arithmetic: Bastrop's real-export source has 15,542 cad_property rows; its stratmap25-landparcels_48021_lp.zip source has 62,257. parcel_record for Bastrop has 62,256 rows, ALL of which overlap the county's cad_property population (verified this session). 62,256 matches the stratmap-fill count (62,257) to within one row. The 15,543 cad_property rows with NO parcel_record match (77,799 total minus 62,256 overlap) match the real-export count (15,542) to within one row.
finding.conclusion: parcel_record for Bastrop was instantiated from the StratMap parcel layer, not from the county's real CAD export -- the same mechanism this lane independently established for Williamson (parcel_record's 282,570 rows are 100% R-prefixed and stratmap-sourced, zero overlap with the 319,480 real numeric CAD accounts). This is ONE consistent mechanism across both counties, not two separate stories: parcel_record tracks the StratMap parcel layer in both. Bastrop looks healthy only because its StratMap rows happen to carry real land_value/land_acres content, while Williamson's are hollow (zero land_value, zero land_acres) -- the instantiation SOURCE is the same; only the CONTENT QUALITY of what StratMap delivered for that county differs.
finding.precisionNote: For Williamson this lane confirmed the mechanism at the prop_id level directly (parcel_record's rows are format-identifiable as R-prefixed, i.e. provably stratmap-sourced). For Bastrop, both the real-export and stratmap sources use plain-numeric prop_ids, so this lane's confirmation is at the COUNT level (the near-exact numeric coincidence above), not a direct per-prop_id identity check against which specific rows parcel_record covers. The count-level match is strong evidence for the same mechanism, stated by doc-repo-26 and consistent with everything else found tonight, but this lane did not independently re-verify Bastrop at the same evidentiary strength as Williamson before recording it -- flagging that distinction for whoever next relies on this.

reframedQuestion: This is no longer 'is there an unexplained ~20% fill gap in Bastrop.' It is: 'is parcel_record supposed to be the StratMap parcel-layer population or the CAD-account population, and does anyone consuming parcel_record know which one they are actually reading.' This also explains why this lane's originally-merged simple-ratio gate produced plausible-looking pass/fail numbers for the three counties it was checked against (Williamson, Caldwell, McLennan): the ratio was comparing two populations (parcel_record's StratMap-sourced rows vs. cad_property's combined real+StratMap population) that only sometimes overlap in quality, and how plausible the resulting ratio looks is an accident of which source each county's StratMap ingest happened to deliver good data from.
ruling: doc-repo-26 is carrying this to the operator as a live Wave 2 question (which population parcel_record is meant to track), not resolving it unilaterally, and not asking this lane to build against it. This lane's caveat from the second addendum stands and is the one doc-repo-26 asked to be preserved above all: the merged gate (PR #100) has only ever been validated against Williamson, Caldwell, and McLennan. Bastrop, Hays, and Travis are untested territory against this gate and must not be treated as validated. The gate's Williamson/Caldwell refusal is itself now understood to rest on a metric under revision -- whether/how to evolve that metric is the operator's call, not something either lane should quietly tune.
action: Documentation only. No code changed, no further live queries run beyond what was already reported in the prior two addenda.
